description: Earth Orchestra is a collaborative team interested in technology, innovation, and creative problem-solving. We welcome motivated members with skills in research, coding, design, data analysis, or presentation.
summary:
When we first started this project, we realised just how intimidating NASA’s data could appear. Its cold, no-nonsense interface was enough to put us off before we had properly explored the website. NASA has a formidable reputation, after all. And so, our aim became to present Earth data in a more approachable and interactive way.
We developed a multisensory website that presents selected Earth data, particularly climate information, through visualisations and sound. By combining the two, we hope to make the data more accessible to users without prior knowledge of the subject.
Users can observe patterns in climate data across the globe while interacting with musical interpretations composed by our team. These melodies can be altered in response to the data, allowing users to explore it through sound as well as sight. Our Learn More sections explain the science behind each visualisation, while the option to combine the melodies lets users listen to the full ensemble. We have also included a text-to-speech feature to make the website more accessible to people with visual impairments.
Ultimately, Earth Orchestra aims to offer a fun, engaging introduction to NASA’s Earth data, sparking curiosity and encouraging users to explore the science further.
details: We used Laravel, MySQL & JavaScript for the coding, utilised Draw Audio for creating the audio and ibisPaint X for the illustrations. The visualisations are made interactable using the color legend provided by NASA. A color picker software is used to color pick from the visualisation which translates over to volume percentage for the premade audio tracks. The change in a particular value, i.e.: temperature, translating over to audio allows the user to visualise the change better than just seeing the numbers on the screen. We also included “Learn more” sections that delve into each of the six topics of our choice(near surface temperature, precipitation, near surface wind speed, near surface humidity, particulate matter and near surface ozone) alongside each of the visualisations to allow users to learn more about each topic. This was done to try to bridge the gap a general user might experience when they first enter the corresponding NASA websites. We believe that simplifying data doesn’t mean dumbing it down, so we aimed to make our explanations scientifically thorough and sound while explaining each term so users aren’t just met with a wall of jargon. We also added a bibliography section with links to the sources so if any user wishes to go directly see the NASA data we referenced, they can do so with ease. We believe this will help make NASA data more accessible and approachable to all.
